newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA CENTRAL BANK TO LET MARKET SET RATES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA CENTRAL BANK TO LET MARKET SET RATES.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Friday it was replacing its main interest rate with the average weighted effective monthly yield of short-term treasury bill auctions held by the finance ministry.

"From January 27 the BNB will announce a main interest rate determined by the average weighted effective monthly yield of short-term government paper auctions held by the finance ministry," the BNB said in a statement.
The new decision will enable commercial banks to link their interest rate policies to the market, the BNB said. The statement gave no further details.

The finance ministry launched daily discount T-bill issues with maturities of one week and four weeks. Their respective yields to maturity are 3.60 percent and 17.45 percent. The ministry has not given their effective monthly yields so far.
"The decision is in line with preparations for implementation of a currency board," said a BNB official, who declined to be named, said earlier.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) proposed last year the introduction of a currency board system which severely curbs financial powers of the government and the central bank.
Under the system, the central bank will not be able to print levs it cannot cover with hard currency reserves, which is expected to remove political pressure from monetary policy.

Bulgaria's central bank raised the main interest rate to a record high of 300 percent annually in September in a bid to support the collapsing lev by curbing panic withdrawals of savings and their conversion into dollars.
Worsening financial crisis prevented the central bank from reducing the rate lower than 180 percent since then.
"If the central interest rate was to be adjusted to the rate of inflation, it should have been hiked even higher, which in turn would have fuelled inflation," said the official.
Inflation for the first 15 days of January alone ran to 30.8 percent, the National Statistics Institute said, and monthly inflation is expected to reach 50 percent.
The lev, which has been in free-fall as a political crisis gained momentum, reached an new historic low on Friday of 910 to the dollar on the interbank market.
"Under the circumstances lifting administrative tabs on the interest rate was the only possible decision," said the official.
The BNB warned earlier on Friday that it lacked the resources to control deepening economic crisis and urged politicians to resolve a deadlock blocking formation of a new government.
